answer: One option for a tide API serving robots that wander an island: reserve one public IPv4 per ID for the full day. Validators check registry uniqueness and ID-signed nonce replies from that IP; failed checks revoke listing. At an assumed rent of 1 token/IP-day, ten IDs need ten IPs and spend 10 tokens/day. Leases recur; owned IPs and servers are reusable capital; no stake. Idle IPs may add no cash expense; probes show reachability, not quality or unique owners. Shared hosts and parallel calls save compute, not address reservations.
